security-spec.md flags this feature as always requiring impact assessment because the validator is 'the deterministic validator that later phases' gates...will trust as their foundation. A validator that best-effort-parses malformed input, executes contract content, or silently passes an invalid contract would weaken every downstream gate built on it' — i.e. fail-closed parsing and content-as-data enforcement are the high-risk design claims here. design.md `## Test Strategy` names a concrete acceptance-test-artifact validation path for exactly this risk: 'acceptance-tests.md の TEST-001..026', explicitly citing fail-closed fixtures (TEST-017: malformed JSON + 10MB oversized input, non-0 exit, no stack trace), type-precedence fixtures (TEST-024, 29 fixtures proving type checks precede pattern/minLength/minItems), and twin-parity fixtures (TEST-013: sh/ps1 exit-code and violation-count agreement). These are concrete, named acceptance test artifacts, satisfying the check's evidence bar. No issues found.
